Trolley Utilization Simulation

The floor

There is no cold start. Work a machine did not finish carries into the next shift, and each plan date is planned on its morning around what every spreader still has left. Machines run at the G2 standard pace. Cutter changeover and moving time are the only lost time added on top ESTIMATES. With every option at its default this is the published model.

The three changes

Tables of the same MO and colour are paired first, each pair spread back-to-back on one spreader. The Job Sequence then counts its tasks and takt time by pairs, and gives each pair to the cut group that keeps the cutters busiest. A partner must already be relaxed to pair, so with fabric relaxing on, different batches pair less often.
Pairs over the floor is the published rule: pairs of one MO and colour are spread across the cut groups. Keep an MO on one cut group is the old behaviour: a whole MO and colour goes to one cut group. It only applies when same-MO sequencing is on.
2 or more lets two batches of one MO and colour share a trolley (2 and 3 behave the same).
How long a part-filled trolley waits for a later table of the same MO, colour and film.
Published takes any trolley of the same MO and colour (two batches at most). Same batch first recalls a trolley already holding the batch just cut, and uses another batch's trolley only if none is waiting. Same batch only never mixes at recall.

How to read this

The published model. With every option at its default, the numbers equal the published model's for the same three changes. The badge above turns green when that holds for the current selection.

Estimates. Fabric arrival, cutter setup and cutter travel are not in the data. They are set by the sliders and every number moves with them. Cutter setup and travel start at the published model's values (they are part of it); fabric arrival is off until you switch it on.

Starved means a spreader had nothing it was allowed to start: its fabric had not relaxed, or the plan date had not begun. Blocked is the spreading table being full (rule G6).

Leftover work. On the carry-over floor every plan date is sequenced on its own morning, around the work each spreader still has committed from the days before. The model runs at the G2 standard pace, so it has spare capacity and the leftover drains faster than on the real floor, which finishes 51% of its tables after their plan date. The model is less late than the real floor.

Output in the same working time. Tables per shift-hour counts the staffed shift window up to the last cut. Set pull-ahead to All to see capacity rather than the calendar.
